design_assessment: Layered authorization: (a) Sanctum auth:sanctum middleware resolves the user from PersonalAccessToken; (b) EnsureUserStatusActive re-checks status fresh from DB per request (defeats token-after-disable attacks); (c) per-route or per-controller `permission:xxx` Spatie middleware enforces Spatie capability; (d) FormRequest authorize() provides a defense-in-depth gate for routes whose namespace is the canonical mount point (OrderRequest checks `tokenCan('kiosk:order')` + namespace `frontend.order.*`). The model is sound. The MISSING coverage is: 16 admin controllers lack __construct middleware AND not all of them are gated at the route — some rely entirely on the FormRequest, which itself has `return true;`. This is the gap class: MenuTemplateController, AnalyticSectionController, DefaultAccessController.

security_concerns.finding: Three POST mutation endpoints (MenuTemplate, AnalyticSection, DefaultAccess) are reachable by any authenticated Sanctum user — no permission gate at controller __construct (verified), no permission middleware at route level (verified routes/api.php:271-274, 384-390, 438-446), FormRequest authorize() returns true (verified). DefaultAccessController::storeOrUpdate mutates the global default-access matrix (affects all branches' default authz binding). MenuTemplateController::store/update/destroy creates/modifies menu templates (catalog-tier mutation). AnalyticSectionController::store/update/destroy modifies tracking pixel sections. A customer's loyalty Sanctum token (created via /api/frontend/loyalty/register) would have any-user power on these endpoints if authenticated.
security_concerns.scenario: Customer registers loyalty account → receives Sanctum token (no ability scoping for default `LoginController` mint = `['*']` per LoginController.php:111+115). Customer's token can call POST /api/admin/menu-template with valid body. EnsureUserStatusActive admits ACTIVE users. apiKey middleware admits any caller carrying the shared x-api-key (NOT a per-user secret). FormRequest authorize() returns true. → 200 Created.
security_concerns.exploitability: HIGH — requires only loyalty signup (unauthenticated /api/frontend/loyalty/register, throttle:5,1) + the shared API_KEY config value (which is a shared secret leaked to every frontend bundle for kiosk handshake — see config/app.php). Production attacker needs to extract API key from kiosk JS bundle (trivially possible).
security_concerns.remediation: Add `permission:settings` middleware on the three prefix groups OR move the gate into controller __construct. Recommended: route-level for consistency with /api/admin/setting/* siblings already gated through their respective controllers. Then add sentinel `RouteCoverage_AdminPermissionGateSentinelTest` asserting every /api/admin/* mutating route resolves to a middleware containing 'permission:' OR a controller method that calls `$user->can(...)`.

security_concerns.finding: PosReceiptPrintController::increment carries `idempotency` middleware but NO permission gate (verified route L840 + controller has no __construct middleware). The endpoint mutates `orders.receipt_print_count` and writes to fiscal `audit_logs` chain. Any authenticated user (including a customer loyalty token) can hit POST /api/admin/pos/orders/{order}/print-receipt. The controller checks `$request->user()->branch_id` and scopes the update to the user's branch (line 37-46), so a customer with branch_id=0 would not match any row (UPDATE returns 0 rows affected → 404 path). Effective exploitation is bounded: attacker would need a branch-pinned user account to drive the increment. But the audit_logs chain entry is written BEFORE the row-not-found check (verified by reading the full controller).
security_concerns.exploitability: MEDIUM — needs branch-pinned token. Less common than admin-zero loyalty token. Audit-chain pollution is the main risk: attacker creates noise in the immutable chain.
security_concerns.remediation: Add `->middleware('permission:pos')` to the route declaration. Defense-in-depth: also add `$this->middleware(['permission:pos'])` in the controller __construct (matching the rest of the Pos/* controllers ParkedOrderController/FloorplanController/CashDrawerSessionController pattern).

security_concerns.finding: All admin controllers that depend on `auth:sanctum + permission:xxx` REQUIRE Sanctum tokens to carry the matching ability. LoginController.php:111 mints admin/staff tokens with abilities=['*'] (wildcard) and Sanctum's PersonalAccessToken::can() returns TRUE for any ability when '*' is present. The channels.php S-R3-P0-G fix correctly avoided this by using token-NAME discrimination (not tokenCan). HOWEVER, no equivalent fix exists for the `abilities:kiosk:order` middleware applied on /kiosk-event + /kiosk/event routes (api.php:1316 + 1362). An admin/staff token (which has abilities=['*']) PASSES `abilities:kiosk:order` check via wildcard. So an admin can spam kiosk events with no permission gate filtering. P3 because admin tokens are already privileged and kiosk event spam is low-impact (rate-limited to 30/min/token).
security_concerns.exploitability: LOW — admin tokens are already high-trust. Kiosk event spam is rate-limited.
security_concerns.remediation: V1.0.2 — narrow LoginController to mint scoped abilities per role (e.g., ['admin:read', 'admin:write'] instead of ['*']). Significant refactor — defer.

security_concerns.finding: Sanctum kiosk-token discriminator on Broadcast channel branch.{branchId} (channels.php:45) checks `$tokenName === 'kiosk-token'` AND verifies `KioskMachine.branch_id === $branchId`. KioskMachineLoginController.php:96-99 deletes ALL existing kiosk-token records before creating a new one (line 96: `$user->tokens()->where('name', 'kiosk-token')->delete()`). Verified intact post 113-commit drift. HOWEVER: a kiosk machine that re-pairs with a NEW branch will have its OLD kiosk-token record purged, but if an in-flight broadcast subscription is open on a different branch (the old one), the connection will continue UNTIL the next reauth. Edge case: pairing-time TOCTTOU on broadcast channels. P2 because the window is bounded by Echo's reconnect interval (default 1 min) and kiosk re-pairing is rare (manual operator action).
security_concerns.remediation: Document in plans/v1-0-2-backlog/. Consider forced Echo re-subscribe broadcast on kiosk re-pair event.

security_concerns.finding: `apiKey` middleware (ApiKeyMiddleware.php:21) reads `config('app.api_key')` and rejects any request without exact-match `x-api-key` header. The api_key is a SHARED single-value secret (no per-client rotation, no per-user scoping). Production frontend bundles (admin SPA, kiosk SPA, customer SPA) all read this same secret from config. ANY frontend bundle download (e.g., kiosk Blade view → kiosk JS bundle) exposes the value in a network-readable form. The middleware was added per AUDIT-P1 for token refresh, but is now applied to the entire /api/auth + /api/admin + /api/frontend + /api/table surfaces. An attacker who scrapes the kiosk JS bundle obtains the api_key and bypasses the gate. This is essentially a shared-secret signature scheme with no rotation.
security_concerns.exploitability: MEDIUM — requires no auth, just network access to the kiosk Blade. Mitigation: api_key alone admits the request to the surface but does NOT replace auth:sanctum — protected routes still require a Sanctum token.
security_concerns.remediation: V1.0.2+ — move to a per-client API key issued at first handshake (kiosk pairing flow) + rotation policy + audit log on key usage. Significant refactor — defer with explicit P2 in V1.0.2 backlog.

security_concerns.finding: Web payment redirect routes in routes/web.php use Route::match(['get','post'], '/payment/{paymentGateway:slug}/{order}/success|fail|cancel', PaymentController) — these are POST endpoints excluded from CSRF (VerifyCsrfToken::except L15-35 covers `/payment/sslcommerz/*` etc.). The CSRF except list does NOT include `/payment/{gateway}/{order}/success` generic pattern — it only enumerates specific gateway slugs (sslcommerz, paytm, cashfree, phonepe, iyzico, pesapal, stripe-webhook, senangpay-webhook). If a new gateway is added (e.g., Adyen, Mollie), the matching success/fail POST callback WILL be CSRF-blocked (HTTP 419) because the new slug isn't on the list. This is a roadmap-defense pattern — works correctly today but is a footgun for future gateway integration.
security_concerns.remediation: V1.0.2 — replace the per-gateway list with a single wildcard `/payment/*/*/success`, `/payment/*/*/fail`, `/payment/*/*/cancel` (consistent with /payment/sslcommerz/* pattern already present). Verify external gateway docs for required CSRF posture (most require CSRF exempt).

security_concerns.finding: Catchall route `/{any}` at routes/web.php:62 returns RootController::index for ANY non-matching URL → serves the SPA Blade (which loads app.js). Combined with the `/admin/pos-v4/{any?}` catchall at L53 → POS V4 Blade. These return HTML 200 even for /api/* paths that don't match any registered api route. This is the documented `silent_html_masquerade` pattern (reference_silent_html_masquerade.md) — a missing api route falls through to SPA Blade with Content-Type text/html. Frontend JS expecting JSON gets HTML and silently fails (axios catches the parse error). Not a security issue but a debugging trap.
security_concerns.remediation: V1.0.2 — add Route::fallback() guard for /api/* paths to return 404 JSON. The SPA catchall stays for non-api URLs.
